- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 5–10 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >15% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 5–10% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day low.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to neutral/positive (e.g., >0.3), model often overreacts; cap forecast increase at +10% from prior 5-day high.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving avg, apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility bias.
